title: Outlook, Teams and More Microsoft Programs Disrupted by Outage
summary: The outage began early Thursday afternoon, causing problems for offices, agencies and individuals around the globe.

Microsoft’s sprawling set of software tools were experiencing widespread outages on Thursday, leaving businesses and workers without crucial tools for hours.


The outage began early Thursday afternoon, as workers and offices around the world began reporting issues with a range of Microsoft 365’s tools and apps, including email and chat software. The problems appeared to be persisting through late Thursday evening.


Between 12:15 p.m. and 1 p.m. Eastern on Thursday, the outage tracker[Downdetector](https://downdetector.com/status/outlook/) showed that more than 130,000 users were experiencing problems with Microsoft Outlook, the workplace messaging app Microsoft Teams, the A.I. assistant Microsoft Copilot and the Microsoft Store.


In[an update](https://x.com/MSFT365Status/status/2121002505911857577) on social media at 5 p.m., Microsoft said it was “opening all pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief.”


The outage affected software used by hundreds of millions of users, impairing corporate offices, government agencies and individuals who rely on the company’s suite of services to send emails, draft letters, conduct virtual meetings and many other daily functions.


The[Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office](https://x.com/arapahoeso/status/2121028236931137547?a=sabnq3DO2IH41YpHhD8&s=46) in Colorado said jail officials could not receive emails to process bond payments for detained individuals because of the outage. A hospital system in Toronto, Unity Health,[said in a statement that](https://unityhealth.to/2026/11/global-microsoft-365-outage-affecting-email-services-at-unity-health-toronto/) its staff members were having trouble sending and receiving email, and asked patients to call instead to arrange appointments. Pennsylvania State University[described](https://www.psu.edu/news/information-technology/story/widespread-microsoft-outage-impacting-penn-state) how its Microsoft services, such as its planner and A.I. agents, were impaired by the outage.


Earlier, Microsoft said that part of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load.”


The company said in a[social media post](https://x.com/MSFT365Status/status/2120938282204688468) around 1 p.m. that “we determined the elevated load isn’t driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable, straining the remaining infrastructure.”


The company said later that it had begun redistributing connection traffic across our broader worldwide infrastructure to help balance the load and that it was restarting affected servers.


“We’re working to safely return them to service,” Microsoft added in[an update](https://status.cloud.microsoft/) .


The outage prompted waves of frustration, anger and glee online. On social media and Reddit, some embraced the system shortage, which allowed them to step away from work, while others expressed concern over how they might be able to work in the future.


Adeel Hassan, a New York-based reporter for The Times, covers breaking news and other topics.


Ishani Desai is a reporter covering breaking news and other topics, and a member of the 2026-27[Times Fellowship](https://www.nytco.com/careers/early-career-opportunities/newsroom-fellowship/) , a program for journalists early in their careers.
